text.headline: Timeline of Czech Republic
text.text: Major events in the history of Czech Republic.

events.headline: Celtic Settlement
events.text: The territory of present-day Czech Republic was inhabited by Celtic tribes, marking the beginning of significant human settlement in the region.

events.headline: Germanic Invasions
events.text: Germanic tribes began to invade and settle in the area, leading to significant cultural and demographic changes.

events.headline: Formation of Great Moravia
events.text: The Slavic state of Great Moravia was established, becoming a significant political entity in Central Europe.

events.headline: Establishment of the Duchy of Bohemia
events.text: The Duchy of Bohemia was established, laying the foundation for the future Kingdom of Bohemia.

events.headline: Golden Bull of Sicily
events.text: The Golden Bull granted the Kingdom of Bohemia hereditary royal status, elevating its importance in the Holy Roman Empire.

events.headline: Charles IV Becomes King
events.text: Charles IV was crowned King of Bohemia, later becoming Holy Roman Emperor, and initiated a period of cultural and economic prosperity.

events.headline: Hussite Wars Begin
events.text: The Hussite Wars erupted following the execution of Jan Hus, leading to significant religious and political upheaval in Bohemia.

events.headline: Habsburg Rule Established
events.text: The Kingdom of Bohemia came under Habsburg rule after the Battle of Mohács, marking a new era of foreign dominance.

events.headline: Defenestration of Prague
events.text: The Defenestration of Prague sparked the Thirty Years' War, a devastating conflict that altered the political landscape of Europe.

events.headline: Battle of White Mountain
events.text: The Battle of White Mountain marked a decisive defeat for the Czech Protestant forces, solidifying Habsburg control over Bohemia.

events.headline: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
events.text: The Austro-Hungarian Compromise established the dual monarchy, impacting the political structure and national identity of Czechs.

events.headline: Czechoslovakia Established
events.text: Czechoslovakia was declared an independent state, marking the end of Austro-Hungarian rule and the beginning of a new nation.

events.headline: Munich Agreement
events.text: The Munich Agreement allowed Nazi Germany to annex parts of Czechoslovakia, leading to increased tensions and eventual occupation.

events.headline: Communist Coup
events.text: The Communist Party seized power in Czechoslovakia, establishing a one-party state that lasted for over four decades.

events.headline: Prague Spring
events.text: The Prague Spring was a period of political liberalization in Czechoslovakia, ultimately suppressed by a Soviet-led invasion.

events.headline: Velvet Revolution
events.text: The Velvet Revolution led to the peaceful overthrow of the Communist regime, restoring democracy in Czechoslovakia.

events.headline: Czech Republic Established
events.text: Czechoslovakia peacefully split into two independent nations, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, marking a new chapter in their histories.

events.headline: Czech Republic Joins EU
events.text: The Czech Republic became a member of the European Union, enhancing its political and economic ties with Europe.

events.headline: Miloš Zeman Elected President
events.text: Miloš Zeman was elected as the first directly elected president of the Czech Republic, marking a significant shift in the political landscape.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted the Czech Republic, leading to health crises and economic challenges.

events.headline: Current Political Landscape
events.text: The Czech Republic continues to navigate its role within the EU and address contemporary issues such as climate change and immigration.
